title: Orioli 2019 newborn orienting · Study 1 auditory comparison
citation: Orioli, G., Santoni, A., Dragovic, D., & Farroni, T. (2019). Identifying peripersonal space boundaries in newborns. Scientific Reports, 9, 9370.
notes: Design inspection for the published static-level orienting task. The outcome is the newborn’s gaze shift after peripheral faces appear. Research playback is blocked.

study_inventory.scope: The pilot and Study 1 are the formal studies. The audio-tactile and auditory-only Study 1 arms used separate groups.

apparatus.speakers: Two loudspeakers positioned beneath the screen, one beneath each half. Sound levels measured at the newborn head position.
apparatus.participant_position: Awake and alert on the experimenter's lap, eyes aligned with the screen center. Holder views a mirrored head-position monitor and cannot see the stimulus presentation.

auditory_stimulus.signal: Static sine tone in a fixed physical setup

trial_schedule.visual_conditions: Central white circle flickers on a black background. Then show two identical infant face images, one on either side, with 1 cm pupil diameter.
trial_schedule.order: Study 1 randomized assignment to audio-tactile or auditory-only arms. Within-arm presentation order is unreported.

response.modality: Video-coded first gaze shift toward either peripheral face
response.anchor: Peripheral faces appear, 5000 ms after central fixation starts.
response.validity: Gaze must be central immediately before peripheral face onset. Offline video coder blind to sound level.

reference_parameters.analysis: At least two valid trials in at least four of five intensity conditions. Contrast the intensity and participant-only models within the auditory arm, and compare across the two assigned stimulation groups.
reference_parameters.preview_scope: Source-defined timing and trial caps are available for inspection. Schedule and playback require the listed sound files together with visual targets, offline gaze scoring and any assigned manual stroke.
implementation_gaps: The 8000 Hz sound assets with verified output calibration at the participant location and original source envelope are unavailable.

A synchronized visual trial scheduler and frame-based gaze response capture are required for fixation, tone and peripheral face events. The source face assets and exact scoring/video settings are unavailable.
A neonatal participant session requires the study-specific equipment, procedures, approvals and trained personnel.

provenance.field: Arm, cohort, intensity allocation and published analysis
Stimulus sequence, gaze coding, apparatus and trial caps
